note: Core Context attaches ctools-style context values to entities and exposes them as runtime contexts. hook_entity_type_alter gives every entity type a 'context' handler: FieldContextHandler (fieldable, reads the no_ui 'context' field type) or SettingsContextHandler (config entities implementing ThirdPartySettingsInterface, reads getThirdPartySetting('core_context','contexts')). Each stored context is a ctools config {type,label,description,value} mapped via ctools.context_mapper->getContextValues() to a \Drupal\Core\Plugin\Context\Context. Providers: core_context (Generic, aggregates tag core_context.context_provider), core_context.canonical_entity (CanonicalEntity), and with layout_builder core_context.layout_builder + a section-component render subscriber. No configure route, permissions, or Drush. Introspection reads a core_context third-party setting stored on the node.article.default entity_view_display; execution attaches a context (verified through the live SettingsContextHandler getContexts() code path) to that display and to the Article node type.

evals.prompt: What does the core_context module do, and how does it make an entity's attached contexts available? Name the entity handler key it registers.
evals.expected_output: It attaches ctools context values to entities and exposes them as runtime contexts. hook_entity_type_alter registers a 'context' entity handler on every entity type (FieldContextHandler for fieldable entities, SettingsContextHandler for config entities), whose getContexts() returns the attached contexts; context provider services surface them at canonical routes and in Layout Builder.

evals.prompt: Where does core_context store the contexts attached to a config entity versus a fieldable entity?
evals.expected_output: On a config entity (ThirdPartySettingsInterface) they live in the third-party setting core_context/contexts (schema core_context.sequence). On a fieldable entity they live in a field of the module's no_ui 'context' field type, read by FieldContextHandler.

evals.prompt: Which context provider services does core_context register, and how do I add my own context provider to it?
evals.expected_output: It registers core_context (Generic, aggregating services tagged core_context.context_provider), core_context.canonical_entity (CanonicalEntity, contexts at canonical entity routes), and with layout_builder core_context.layout_builder. Add your own by registering a ContextProviderInterface service tagged core_context.context_provider.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, a core_context context has been attached to the Article default view display. Inspect the live configuration and state the value of that attached context.
On this Drupal site, a single core_context context is attached to the Article default view display. Inspect the live configuration and state the machine key/name of that context.

On this Drupal site, use core_context to attach a context to the Article content type's default view display (node.article.default). The context must have the key 'cc_task', data type 'string', and value 'built'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set third_party_settings.core_context.contexts.cc_task = {type: string, label: ..., description: '', value: 'built'} on core.entity_view_display.node.article.default (e.g. $display->setThirdPartySetting('core_context','contexts', ['cc_task' => ['type'=>'string','label'=>'...','description'=>'','value'=>'built']])->save()), so the display's 'context' handler getContexts() returns a cc_task context valued 'built'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use core_context to attach a context to the Article content type entity itself (the node_type config entity 'article'). The context must have the key 'cc_ntype', data type 'string', and value 'typed'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set third_party_settings.core_context.contexts.cc_ntype = {type: string, label: ..., description: '', value: 'typed'} on the article node type (NodeType is a ThirdPartySettingsInterface config entity handled by SettingsContextHandler), so node_type's 'context' handler getContexts() returns a cc_ntype context valued 'typed'.
